intro: Weak declension of the adjective: when the definite article already clearly marks gender and case, the adjective takes only two possible endings: **-e** or **-en**.

frases.estudio: Hast du den neuen Mietvertrag für die Wohnung schon gelesen?
frases.alumno: Have you already read the new rental contract for the flat?
analisis: have you read the new rental contract?

frases.estudio: Ja, der freundliche Vermieter hat mir alle Klauseln genau erklärt.
frases.alumno: Yes, the friendly landlord explained all the clauses to me in detail.
analisis: hat mir alle Klauseln genau erklärt
explained all the clauses to me in detail

frases.estudio: Das helle Wohnzimmer und die ruhige Lage im Altbau haben uns sofort überzeugt.
frases.alumno: The bright living room and the quiet location in the period building convinced us straight away.
analisis: the quiet location in the period building

frases.estudio: Stimmt, aber wir müssen die hohen Nebenkosten im Winter beachten.
frases.alumno: That's true, but we have to bear in mind the high service charges in winter.
analisis: the high service charges in winter

texto: After the definite article (**der**, **die**, **das** and their declined variants), the adjective takes the so-called weak ending: **-e** in the four singular cases not marked obliquely (masculine nominative: **der neue Mietvertrag**, neuter nominative: **das helle Zimmer**, feminine nominative: **die ruhige Lage**, and feminine and neuter accusative: **die moderne Küche**, **das sonnige Wohnzimmer**).

In all other cases of the table (masculine accusative, all datives, all genitives and the entire plural), the invariable ending of the adjective is **-en**: **den neuen Mietvertrag**, **dem freundlichen Vermieter**, **der renovierten Wohnung**, **die hohen Nebenkosten**.

pregunta.texto: What ending does the adjective take after the definite article in the masculine accusative?

opciones.texto: -en
opciones.explicacion: In masculine accusative after «den», the adjective invariably takes the weak ending «-en».

opciones.texto: -e
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-e» is only used in the masculine nominative and in the neuter and feminine nominative/accusative.

opciones.texto: -es
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-es» belongs to the strong declension without article or to the mixed neuter declension after «ein».

frase.texto: Wir unterschreiben heute den neu___ Mietvertrag.

opciones.texto: en
opciones.explicacion: After the accusative article «den», the masculine adjective requires the weak ending «-en».

opciones.texto: e
opciones.explicacion: «neue» would correspond to the nominative case, not to the accusative marked by «den».

opciones.texto: em
opciones.explicacion: «neuem» would correspond to a strong dative without article, never after «den».

pregunta.texto: Which qualities of the property motivated a favourable decision?

frase.texto: Das helle Wohnzimmer und die ruhige Lage im Altbau haben uns sofort überzeugt.

opciones.texto: The remarkable brightness of the main living room and the peaceful atmosphere of the period building proved decisive.
opciones.explicacion: The two essential attributes described are highlighted: spatial brightness and quiet in the building.

opciones.texto: The flat was flatly rejected for lacking ventilation and suffering constant street noise.
opciones.explicacion: It states the exact opposite of «helle» and «ruhige Lage».

opciones.texto: The tenants preferred to move to a new-build because of the lack of space in the rooms.
opciones.explicacion: The text expressly indicates that the flat in the Altbau convinced them straight away.

pregunta.texto: Why does the adjective end in «-e» in «die ruhige Lage» and in «-en» in «der ruhigen Lage»?

opciones.texto: Because in the feminine singular nominative it takes «-e», but in the feminine dative or genitive it changes to «-en».
opciones.explicacion: After the definite article, all the indirect cases (dative/genitive) always take the ending «-en».

opciones.texto: Because the adjective must agree obligatorily with the plural of the main verb.
opciones.explicacion: «Lage» is a feminine singular noun; the ending follows case inflection.

opciones.texto: Because «Lage» changes its grammatical gender depending on the verb tense of the sentence.
opciones.explicacion: Grammatical gender is inherent to each noun and remains invariable.

frase.texto: Der Mieter bewohnt das hell___ Zimmer zur Gartenseite.

opciones.texto: e
opciones.explicacion: In neuter singular accusative after «das», the adjective takes the weak ending «-e».

opciones.texto: en
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-en» after «das» appears only in oblique cases such as the dative («dem hellen»).

opciones.texto: es
opciones.explicacion: The strong marking is not duplicated when the definite article «das» already makes the gender explicit.

pregunta.texto: What warning does Karin raise regarding household finances?

frase.texto: Karin: Stimmt, aber wir müssen die hohen Nebenkosten im Winter beachten.

opciones.texto: It warns about the budget impact of the high additional charges during the cold months.
opciones.explicacion: «hohen Nebenkosten» directly refers to heating and common expenses in winter.

opciones.texto: It recommends giving up the flat because the landlord refuses to install heating.
opciones.explicacion: The flat is not rejected; it only warns about the amount of the additional costs.

opciones.texto: It assures that the service charges are fully covered by a state subsidy.
opciones.explicacion: The dialogue doesn't mention any external help, but the need to pay attention to the cost.

pregunta.texto: Which of the following sentences flawlessly applies the weak declension after the definite article?

opciones.texto: Der neue Hausmeister kontrolliert die moderne Heizanlage im Keller.
opciones.explicacion: «Der neue» applies -e in masculine nominative, and «die moderne» applies -e in feminine accusative after the definite article.

opciones.texto: Der neuen Hausmeister kontrolliert die modernen Heizanlage im Keller.
opciones.explicacion: It wrongly uses the ending «-en» in singular nominative and accusative where «-e» is required.

opciones.texto: Der neu Hausmeister kontrolliert die modern Heizanlage im Keller.
opciones.explicacion: It omits the obligatory adjective endings in German attributive inflection.
